title: Nefertiti
summary: Nefertiti was chief consort ("Great Royal Wife") of the 18th Dynasty pharaoh Akhenaten, who founded the capital Akhetaten, now Amarna, around 1340 BCE. Her limestone bust, dated c. 1340 BCE, was found in the workshop of the sculptor Thutmose at Amarna in 1912 and is now in the Neues Museum, Berlin. Her mummy has not been found.

uncertainty.note: Her own dates are not given on the opened pages; the span uses Akhenaten's reign (about 1351–1334 BCE) as a proxy, converted to astronomical years.

as_recorded.value: c. 1340 BCE (bust and founding of Amarna)

where.modern_name: Tell el-Amarna (ancient Akhetaten), Asyut Governorate, Egypt (pinned to the royal capital where she lived and her bust was found)
where.historical_name: Akhetaten, capital of Egypt under Akhenaten, 18th Dynasty, New Kingdom

importance.justification: Chief consort of Akhenaten; her bust from Amarna is among the best-known works of ancient Egyptian art.
